old_title: Australia v South Africa LIVE: Latest updates as Wallabies host Springboks
new_title: Australia v South Africa LIVE: Result and reaction as Wallabies stun Springboks

A busy year of international action continues for Australia and South Africa as the two sides collide in an intriguing one-off Test in Perth.
The Springboks are heavily changed from the side that secured a 3-1 Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series success in their last outing two weeks ago, with Rassie Erasmus taking the opportunity to assess the depth of his squad. A trip to Western Australia is valuable preparation for next year's World Cup, too, with the defending champions likely to play twice in Perth during the course of that tournament.
The Wallabies, meanwhile, will relish an opportunity to test themselves against the best having made an encouraging start to life under Les Kiss. Time is tight to find their groove before a World Cup on home soil but a statement win here could prove just the jolt they need with little more than 12 months to go.
Follow all of the latest from Perth with our live blog below:
Australia 42-17 South Africa, 68 minutes
Eben Etzebeth has left the field, we're unsure what the issue is, much debate on the touchline.
Australia 42-17 South Africa, 68 minutes
It is worth underlining this is not a full-strengt Boks outfit, but Australia won't care, this is a statement and spikes the momentum heading into a home World Cup year.
Could they be a threat?
TRY! Australia 42-17 South Africa (Max Jorgensen), 64 minutes
Can you believe it!?
A massive statement, Moodie drops it, then Jorgensen is ruthless, express speed, you can't catch him with that much space.
What a try and this match is over, surely?
TRY! Australia 37-17 South Africa (Harry Wilson), 60 minutes
No try... Australia thought they had a game-clincher, Wilson couldn't get it down.
The skipper backed in, but his ankle was just out of touch. Still, Australia pile on the pressure, Paisami is there, now just a metre.
TRY! Wilson has his moment, the Perth crowd roar! Wilson picked it up, dunking it over some bodies.
Australia 30-17 South Africa, 57 minutes
Australia outgaining South Africa with 255m to 196m.
An Australia scrum now, which could be vital, it's out neatly and Paisami clatters into the Boks wall.
Potter fed on the wing, Hooper is there, Australia can sense the hammer blow. Wilson within a few metres.
Another scrum, this is gripping, the Boks surviving, immense defence.
Australia 30-17 South Africa, 55 minutes
Ikitau is off, that right ankle is in a bad way. Potter comes in.
Australia with the ball again, but happy to go long and Jorgensen claims, beating Horn, just remarkable, the Boks concede more territory.
Potter out wide on the left now, South Africa scrambling. The Boks rip the ball out.
Australia 30-17 South Africa, 52 minutes
A scrum in midfield and Australia remain lively in this one.
But Ikitau with a blow and hobbling on a dodgy ankle, Harry Potter ready to enter the game.
Lonergan can kick another for the Wallabies... Another three, the Boks now down 13 points. Well, well, well...
Australia 27-17 South Africa, 47 minutes
That could be vital... Lonergan splits the posts, Wallabies up by 10.
Now then, the bomb squad are ready, can they flip this game?
Australia 24-17 South Africa, 42 minutes
We're back underway in Perth, the Boks go high early.
But Sua'ali'i was brave, up early and tapped the ball back. But the Boks have the penalty, Pollard dumps the ball deep into the Aussie half...
A line-out, but Australia counter the maul and win the ball back. Huge result from the Wallabies pack.
HT Australia 24-17 South Africa
And breathe, a cracker here and South Africa are down, Australia up 24-17.
Ambitious rugby from the Wallabies, Ikitau with a brace, flashes of brilliance from the Boks, but Wright's magic touch unlocked the world champions on the stroke of half-time.
A gripping second half to come...

Australia held on with 11 men in a dramatic finish to beat a second-string South Africa outfit 42-38 at Perth Stadium on Sunday and extend their unbeaten run to five games since new coach Les Kiss took over in late July. Skipper Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan, Joseph Suaalii and Hunter Paisami were all shown yellow cards in the last 10 minutes as the world champions cut a 25-point deficit down to four at the final whistle.
Australia had looked to be cruising after centre Len Ikitau's double and tries from flyhalf Ben Donaldson, number eight Wilson and winger Max Jorgensen combined with 17 points from the boot of scrumhalf Ryan Lonergan gave them a 42-17 lead after 65 minutes. The last 10 minutes threatened to undo all their earlier good work but the Wallabies will move on to back-to-back tests against the All Blacks in October without a loss in six games, their best unbeaten run since 2017.
South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus had made 13 changes to his lineup from the team that completed the gruelling 3-1 series victory over New Zealand earlier this month but stacked his bench with first-choice players as an insurance policy. It almost paid off in the frantic last 10 minutes, but scores from hooker Johan Grobbelaar, winger Edwill van der Merwe, scrumhalf Morne van den Berg, prop Ox Nche as well as a penalty try were not quite enough.
The visitors scored the first try after Handre Pollard and Lonergan had exchanged early penalties with Grobbelaar rolling over the line on the back of a rolling maul. Australia responded with two tries from Ikitau in three minutes, the first from close range and the second after winger Suaalii had disrupted the restart and the ball bounced back to the lurking centre. The Springboks responded almost immediately to lock up the scores again at 17-17, flyhalf Pollard's long pass exposing a hole in the Australian backline defence and Van der Merwe showing his pace to finish the move.
A slanted crosskick from Wallabies fullback Tom Wright gave Jorgensen some space to run shortly before halftime, however, and Australia recycled patiently when the winger was held up shy of the line with Donaldson going over unopposed in the corner after 14 phases. Lonergan extended Australia's lead with his second penalty eight minutes into the second half, prompting Erasmus to bring on all eight of his replacements, and added a third three-pointer after 54 minutes to make it 30-17.
The Wallabies were now taking the Springboks on up front and tapped a penalty close to the line just before the hour mark with Wilson forcing his way over and slapping the ball down for a try. The Springboks stormed back to try and cut the 20-point deficit but when Canan Moodie spilled the ball, Jorgensen was on hand to scoop it up and sprint 60 metres for Australia's fifth try. Reuters.
Springboks coach admits they 'rolled the dice' in Australia
Rassie Erasmus noted: "When you're 25 points behind, there's nobody else to blame but yourself. We rolled the dice a bit, and some guys haven't played a lot together in a long time, but it's not an excuse.
"We picked the team, and we had a game plan, and I thought we had a chance at the end, but the better team won on the night. It's sad to lose, but it's not because we've been together too long. It's because we didn't play well enough."
Rassie Erasmus in honest assessment of Springboks
"For us, we lost in a Springbok jersey against Australia, and with all the disruptions, we have nobody else to blame but ourselves for the result," said Erasmus.
"I know the technology failed a bit, the clock kept running and didn't stop at times for example, but that didn't influence how we played. We controlled that. We didn't play well enough tonight to beat a stronger team."
Wallabies legend reacts to huge win over South Africa
Michael Hooper: "A few text messages, one was, 'what sport are we watching?'
"They deserves to be further ahead, the yellow cards were harsh. They controlled the possession.
"The forced South Africa into discipline issues, they were up for it. So happy to hear the words from Harry Wilson, what it means to them."
Wallabies captain Harry Wilson reacts to historic win over world champions
"I'm so proud of the group, mate, we're excited, up for it, that first 70 minutes, way we played, exactly what we wanted, so proud of the boys," says Harry Wilson.
"We knew as a forward pack, we had to step up, we had to back ourselves, we have some special players, and in space, they can do special things."
Boks captain Andre Esterhuizen reacts to gripping test match
Boks captain Andre Esterhuizen: "It was a very intense game, quite quick for a test match. It let us down, we let them in too much. It hurt us.
"We were too disjointed, discipline, the key factor that let us down.
"The last 18-19 weeks, we know each other well, the plan well, it's about executing. Proud of the fight at the end, but we need to be better than that."
FT: Australia 42-38 South Africa
AUSTRALIA SURVIVE, AUSTRALIA WIN!
South Africa thought they had one last chance, but obstruction and the Wallabies boot it into touch. Stunning.
TRY! Australia 42-38 South Africa (Ox Nche), 80 minutes
Etzebeth held up, his body is over the try line.
Marx bundling through the Australia backline, SOUTH AFRICA TRY!
Nche sprints back, the conversion is good, time for a restart, can you believe this?
Australia 42-31 South Africa, 78 minutes
This is chaotic!
Esterhuizen thought he was about to score, Wright gathers the loose ball, booting upfield.
Australia are desperate, up by 11, with 11 men on the field.
The Boks overthrow the line-out, remarkable, a lifeline for the Wallabies.
